title: habitat research insight
description: The YAML front matter of a research/insights/<id>.md file. One distilled finding about the people who use the product, with the evidence behind it and what it implies for design. Rules elsewhere cite it by id, so an agent can reason from the finding when no rule covers the case. Never put raw transcripts or personal data here: distil, anonymise, and link to the source.

id.description: A short stable id that rules cite, e.g. 'INS-004'.

status.description: 'draft' until a researcher has checked it; 'reviewed' once they have; 'retired' when newer research has replaced it (add supersededBy).

insight.description: The finding in one or two plain sentences, about people and what they do, not about the interface.

confidence.description: strong: consistent across studies or a well-run study. emerging: seen, but in few people or one study. hunch: the team believes it but has not tested it. Agents weigh insights by this.

evidence.description: Where the finding comes from. Link to the source rather than copying it.

method.description: e.g. interviews, usability test, survey, analytics, support tickets, diary study.

participants.description: How many people, e.g. 12, or '4,000 sessions'.

date.description: When the study ran (YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD).

link.description: Where the source lives: a research repository, a report, a document.

people.description: Who it applies to. If research/people/ has files, use their ids.

journeys.description: The core journeys from DESIGN.md it matters for.

implications.description: What it means for design, in plain words. The rules that follow from it cite this insight's id.

supersededBy.description: For a retired insight, the id of the one that replaced it.

owner.description: Who answers questions about this finding.

lastReviewed.description: When a person last confirmed it still holds (YYYY-MM-DD).
